nodes.label: Deposit hold reconciliation against Stripe (read side)
Rationale: card authorisations expire silently and nothing in the codebase notices (GMT incident, Aug 2026)
PaymentIntent status to deposit_hold_status truth table (only four statuses are conclusive)
Hold status vocabulary is pinned to the rentals.deposit_hold_status CHECK constraint
Response contract: status is ALWAYS a string, with a never-persisted 'none' sentinel
Editor-only authorization shared by the five deposit-hold money paths
Rationale: verify_jwt only proves 'a session on this project' and booking CUSTOMERS hold one, so a tenant/role guard runs before the rental read
Rationale: never persist a moving fallback expiry, it would starve the refresh cron
Record-anchored Stripe account resolution via rentals.platform_account
Rationale: an unresolvable Stripe context is reported as needsReview, because a mid-OAuth UAE tenant would otherwise 500 on every verify
deposit_hold_links verify ledger: one fully-replaced row per (rental, attempt, action)
Rationale: the ledger row is written AFTER the write attempt so `outcome` describes what actually landed
Audit and clock writes are non-fatal by design (supabase-js resolves on DB error but REJECTS on transport failure)
Orphaned PaymentIntent reported as needsReview, never concluded as released funds
Worker-owned row guard: 'processing' and 'refreshing' are never overwritten
Compare-and-set anchored to both hold status and the probed PaymentIntent id
Rationale: a status-only CAS would let a stale 'canceled' probe double-authorise the renter's card
Gotcha: PostgREST .or() on .update() mis-qualifies the column, so branch on .is()/.eq()
A lost CAS re-reads the row and reports the CURRENT state instead of the stale conclusion
Forward-only re-stamp of deposit_hold_chain_expires_at from the rental's live end date
Rationale: extending a rental moves end_date without re-placing the hold, so the chain would terminate on the ORIGINAL end date while the car is still out
Gotcha: expiries are compared as instants because Postgres '+00:00' and toISOString() '.000Z' never string-match
Rationale: a NULL expiry means 'we do not know this is alive' and sorts most urgent for the refresher
A persisted deadline carries its provenance: deposit_hold_expiry_source, extended_auth, window_seconds
A deliberate 'released' is never downgraded to 'expired' (it records a human's action)
Operator-facing plain-English outcome messages for a dead, live or in-flight hold
AI insurance certificate legitimacy audit (gpt-4o vision, 0-100 score plus field extraction)
Score-to-status policy: not-insurance or <40 rejected, 40-69 flagged, 70+ verified
insurance_verifications status lifecycle: processing -> verified / flagged / rejected / failed
Rationale: the OpenAI usage logger is inlined (mirrors _shared/openai.ts) so this function can be deployed standalone
Per-tenant OpenAI cost accounting for document audits (hardcoded per-model $/Mtok table)
PDF certificates are refused with 422: OpenAI vision cannot read them
Supabase Storage URL parsing so public/signed certificate objects are pulled with service-role rights
Chunked (8KB) base64 encoding so a multi-megabyte certificate image does not blow the argument stack
Every failure path stamps status='failed' plus ai_error on the verification row so the operator sees why
ai_findings records the model, flags and reasoning alongside the score so a verdict stays explainable
Email OTP verification and Supabase Auth email confirmation
Single-use OTP: the row is deleted on success and on expiry so a code can never be replayed
Verifying an OTP also flips email_confirmed_at on the Supabase Auth user (admin.updateUserById)
Gap: MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5 is declared but never enforced — no attempt counter and no rate limit
Gap: the auth user is resolved by scanning admin.listUsers() rather than a direct email lookup
Gap: tenant_id scoping is optional, so a code can be matched without a tenant boundary
Server-side session-revocation check for the portal session guard
Fail-open contract: only a definitive 'no such session' can log an operator out
Rationale: postgres.js crashes in the Supabase edge runtime, so auth.sessions is read via a SECURITY DEFINER rpc over PostgREST
JWT payload decoded without signature verification because the platform already verified it (verify_jwt = true)
session_is_active (SECURITY DEFINER rpc over auth.sessions)
Public short-code offer resolution (verify_jwt = false, Spec Section 6.6)
Offer view tracking: view_count, first/last_viewed_at and a pending -> viewed status bump
lead.offer_opened fires exactly once, on first view, alongside a lead_activity row
Lazy expiry: an offer expires on read, emits lead.offer_expired and returns 410
Vehicle rates are selected under both the legacy and current column names (daily_rate and rate_daily)
The offer payload carries show_prices / deposit_amount / date_flex_days so the public page renders exactly what the operator chose to reveal
Void a duplicate or stale unpaid payment link
Deliberately narrower than reject_payment: touches only the payments row, never the rental or vehicle
Manual tenant-isolation check because the service-role client bypasses RLS
Rationale: staff can belong to several tenants, so ALL app_users rows are read (maybeSingle would falsely 401 them)
Fail-closed guards: nothing carrying real money can be voided
Server mirror of the portal's isCaptured() paid-state rule (an uncaptured pre-auth is NOT captured)
A deposit hold is refused here and routed to the deposit release flow instead
An unpaid link that somehow has payment_applications is refused — voiding would silently un-apply money
Best-effort Stripe Checkout session expiry so a still-live link cannot be paid after voiding
Soft-cancel to status 'Reversed' / capture_status 'cancelled', never a hard delete, so history stays auditable
Concurrency guard: the update is anchored to an unpaid row and 409s if a webhook captured it mid-flight

tenants table

release-deposit-hold edge function

Lead offer link lifecycle: short code minted, publicly viewed, event-bussed, then accepted or expired
Portal session revocation chain: force-logout deletes the GoTrue session, verify-session detects it, the client guard signs the operator out
